name: dsh-launcher-panel
description: Start DeepSeek Harness (dsh) and open its web UI in VS Code's built-in browser.

dsh.runMode.description: How to run DeepSeek Harness: 'pnpm' installs dsh into a launcher-managed location and runs 'pnpm exec dsh web'; 'source' runs a local checkout via tsx. Normally set with the mode pill in the panel. Machine-local: source mode depends on a checkout and toolchain that exist on this machine, so the choice is not synchronized.

dsh.npmChannel.description: Which npm dist-tag pkg mode installs @deepseek-ai/dsh from on first install, and which version the Update button targets: 'latest' (stable), 'next' (release candidates), or 'alpha' (alphas). An installed dsh always starts as-is — the channel never downgrades or auto-upgrades it. Source mode ignores this and always tracks the newest official dsh-v<version> git tag.

dsh.pkgPath.description: Optional: custom directory where pkg mode installs dsh. When empty, the extension uses a managed default location. Machine-local path: not synchronized across machines.

dsh.srcPath.description: Optional: path to an existing deepseek-harness clone for source mode. When empty, the extension clones the repo automatically. Machine-local path: not synchronized across machines.

dsh.nodePath.description: Path to node.exe. Leave empty to use the node on PATH. Machine-local path: not synchronized across machines.

dsh.port.description: Legacy single-instance port. Read once to create the default instance in dsh.instances; ports are otherwise assigned by the launcher. Machine-local: ports belong to one machine and are not synchronized.
dsh.port.deprecationMessage: Multi-instance management uses dsh.instances; dsh.port is only read once to migrate the default instance.

dsh.instancePortBase.description: Five-digit starting point for auto-assigned instance ports. The first new instance gets base+1 (31001 by default), the next base+2, and so on. The migrated Default instance keeps port 3080; ports are not edited in the panel.

dsh.autoOpenBrowser.description: Automatically open the browser after dsh starts. Turn off to keep your current tab (the official page shows a reconnect prompt); the Start button's 'New Tab' click still opens one per dsh.browser.

dsh.browser.description: Which browser to open the UI in. 'built-in' uses VS Code's Simple Browser (falls back to external if disabled); 'external' opens the system browser.

dsh.hideConsole.description: Run the DSH server in a hidden console so neither it nor the tool subprocesses (bash/pwsh) flash a cmd window. Turn off to show it for debugging.

dsh.clearServerLogOnStart.description: Clear the server log file at the start of each launch so it only contains the current run.

dsh.sourceDebug.description: In source mode, enable NODE_DEBUG=module to print module-loading progress (very verbose; the console shows a periodic count, full detail is in the server log).

dsh.instances.description: DSH instances managed by the launcher. Each entry is a runtime coordinate: a DSH_HOME (home), a profile inside it, and a Web UI port. Empty home means the default home. Instances are machine-local.

id.description: Stable instance id; generated by the launcher.

home.description: DSH_HOME for this instance; empty uses the default home.

port.description: Web UI port; unique across configured instances.

dsh.activeInstance.description: Initial active instance for a newly opened window (each window keeps its own active instance while open). Empty falls back to the first instance.

dsh.instanceBrand.description: Show the instance name under the DeepSeek Harness wordmark in the Web UI. The launcher maintains a tiny local client bundle in each instance profile; no manual plugin install is needed.

scripts.verify: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run compile && npm run package
